notes:
- The theme is built from the cover's own pixels: Opening a title now reads its cover art and derives the app's colour from the pixels you are looking at, the way Material You reads a wallpaper, instead of trusting AniList's single server-computed average of the whole file. A 128px decode is binned, scored by Material 3's rules - chroma is rewarded, hues are counted as a neighbourhood, and greys are dropped - so a black-and-white cover falls back to AniList's colour and then to the brand blue rather than producing a grey app.
- Every Material role is now a real tonal palette: The old builder interpolated in HSL, where lightness is not luminance, so contrast and container relationships depended on the seed. A pure-Kotlin HCT/CAM16 engine now builds tonal-spot palettes at Material's fixed tones: 40/80 for primary, 10/90 for containers, 6/98 for surfaces and 30/80 for secondary text. Buttons, chips, the app bar and the sheet all move together because every one of the 36 scheme roles is generated, not just the handful that used to change.
